title: Task Cooldown Schedule
statement:
Find the fewest time slots needed to run every task when identical tasks must be spaced apart.

Contract
- `tasks` is a string of uppercase letters `A`-`Z`; each letter is a kind of task and each task takes exactly one slot. It may be empty.
- Two tasks of the same letter must have at least `cooldown` slots between them. Different letters have no restriction.
- Tasks may run in any order, and a slot may be left idle. Return the minimum total number of slots, idle ones included; an empty string needs `0`.
- `cooldown >= 0`. Throw `IllegalArgumentException` for a negative cooldown.

Examples
- `AAABBB` with cooldown `2` takes 8 slots: `A B _ A B _ A B`.
- `ABCD` with cooldown `3` needs no idle slots, so it takes 4.
- `AAAB` with cooldown `2` takes 7 slots: `A B _ A _ _ A`.
hints: Always run the task type with the most work remaining that is not cooling down; idle only when nothing is ready.
A max-heap of remaining counts plus a queue of cooling tasks simulates this greedy schedule. Notice what the busiest letter alone forces.

The most frequent task, repeated `max` times with `tied` letters sharing that count, forces `(max - 1) * (cooldown + 1) + tied` slots; other tasks fit in the gaps or extend the schedule, so the answer is the larger of that and `tasks.length()`. Intended complexity: O(n) time to count letters and O(1) space because the alphabet has 26 letters (the heap simulation costs O(n log 26) time).
inputSyntax: Input: the task letters A-Z with no spaces, then the cooldown, for example: AAABBB 2
